items.title: bug-bash
items.description: Bug bash one area of a codebase: parallel read-only hunters, every finding verified by you, then fixed through `file-and-fix`.

items.title: code-review
items.description: "Two-axis review of a pinned change or a Spec: Standards (the repo's documented standards) and Spec (what the Issue asked for), by one independent reviewer role (`ticket-reviewer` for a change, `spec-reviewer` for a Spec). Use to review a branch, work in progress, \"review since X\", a candidate before `slipjay land` (a Spec's assembled landing, a later fix to it, or other work), or a Spec someon…

items.title: delivery-digest
items.description: Summarise in plain English what the user shipped, feature by feature, over a day or other window. Use for the daily digest, or when asked what got done, shipped or landed today, yesterday or this week.

items.title: dependency-updater
items.description: Aggressively update project dependencies, including compatible majors, adapt code/config where needed, and verify the resulting dependency set works together. Reads and maintains the repository's docs/dependencies.md stack file. Use for dependency upgrades, stale packages, vulnerabilities, or compatibility repair.

items.title: diagnose-bug
items.description: Diagnose a bug with the read-only `advisor` role when your own diagnosis leaves the cause unexplained, or straight away when the bug is in code you wrote this session. Use for a bug report, a failing behaviour or "why is X broken", before designing a fix.

items.title: domain-modeling
items.description: Forge and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.

items.title: file-and-fix
items.description: Hand a bug or chore you noticed, but that isn't your current task, to a cheap chore worker. It checks Forge for a duplicate, fixes it in its own workspace and hands back a commit for you to check and land; anything it can't fix, it records once. Use whenever you notice a defect while doing other work, before any `weave_forge_create` or `gh issue create`, and when Henry says "file that", "log it"…

items.title: github-issues
items.description: "Shape and reconcile GitHub Specs and Tickets: hierarchy, blockers, labels and readiness, in repositories whose tracker is GitHub (references/tracker.md)."

items.title: lead
items.description: Implement and own delivery of one Spec, or an Arc of Specs, end to end. Use when the user says "lead", "work", "run spec N", "orchestrate", "clear the backlog", or asks to build a shaped Spec or take an Arc to its outcome. Not for creating or revising intent (use `shape`).

items.title: phi-browser
items.description: "Browser work in Phi: opening pages, interacting with websites, scraping, screenshots and web-app checks. Use for browser tasks from Mac or VPS; follow global guidance for context selection and lifecycle."

items.title: prototype
items.description: Build a disposable prototype to answer one design or behaviour question quickly. Prefer a small self-contained HTML prototype; use the real app only when app context is necessary to get trustworthy evidence.

items.title: reddit
items.description: Find Reddit discussions, read threads and account activity, prepare drafts, and publish specifically authorised posts or replies through Henry's logged-in browser.

items.title: shape
items.description: Investigate, create or revise a Spec's intent instead of writing a plan file. Use when the user is working out what to build, asks to plan or scope work, edits an existing Spec, or enters plan mode, even without saying "shape". Not for implementing shaped work (use `lead`).

items.title: t3-fork-install
items.description: Install a T3 Code change into Henry's desktop app, the fork build `T3 Peach.app`. Use when a task's work has landed on `t3peach`, when asked to install, ship to the app, or "build it" for T3 Code, and from `t3-fork-rebase` after a merge.

items.title: tickets
items.description: Rare exception: break a Spec into Tickets only when separately owned work must land in a required order that one run cannot hold. Splitting a Spec is not a normal step; `shape` and `lead` do not run this by default.

items.title: unattended
items.description: Stance for when the user is away: finish `shape` or `lead` work without asking. Use when the user says "unattended", "hands-free" or "while I'm away".

items.title: wait-what
items.description: "Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it."

items.title: writing-for-agents
items.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

items.title: contribution-triage
items.description: Enforce T3 Code's PR contribution policy by closing ineligible submissions and triggering Macroscope review for eligible work within authorized scope. Supports explicit dry runs. Use for contribution moderation, not installation diagnostics or a full code review.

items.title: t3-fork-rebase
items.description: Bring an upstream T3 Code nightly tag into the fork's `t3peach` branch: merge it, reconcile it against the fork's recorded differences, and land it through SlipJay. Run when the fork-nightly webhook starts a thread with a tag, or when asked to update the fork to a nightly.

items.title: test-t3-app
items.description: Test T3 Code's web and desktop UI through its built-in Browser panel against isolated development state. Use for browser verification, browser pairing recovery, and test fixtures. Use test-t3-mobile for native mobile verification.

items.title: test-t3-mobile
items.description: Test T3 Code's native iOS and Android app through its Device panel and returned AgentDevice command. Use for mobile verification, native-client builds, Metro launch, and mobile pairing against isolated development state.

items.title: docs/internals/terminal-runtime.md
items.description: Terminal runtime. The environment server owns PTYs, session lifetime, and retained output. Every client, including the desktop renderer, attaches through the environment connection. This lets clients reconnect or share a running session. Renderer choices stay local to each client and do not change terminal contracts.

items.title: docs/internals/voice-input.md
items.description: Voice input. Transcription edits a composer draft. It does not submit an agent turn. Audio is temporary client input, and only normal message submission sends the resulting text. The current implementation transcribes locally on supported iOS devices; environment-backed transcription is not implemented.

items.title: docs/internals/web-ui.md
items.description: Web UI. Controls come from [`components/ui`](../../apps/web/src/components/ui). [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#architecture-and-implementation) says how to use and extend them.

items.title: docs/operations/agent-delegation.md
items.description: Managed agent delegation. `t3 agent` and the delegation tools resolve roles and models from a central agent policy kept outside T3 Code, in the agent-config repository (`roles/policy.json` and the role briefs in `roles/`). Nothing is enabled until the server is told where that checkout is.

items.title: docs/operations/android-notifications.md
items.description: Android notifications. The Android app receives Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) data messages. The relay sends them directly through FCM HTTP v1; an Expo Push account is not required.

items.title: docs/user/background-service.md
items.description: Running T3 Code in the background. On Linux and macOS, T3 Code can run as a service for your user so you do not need to keep a terminal open.

items.title: docs/user/browser-import.md
items.description: Import browser sessions. The desktop app can import cookies from another browser so you can reuse its signed-in sessions in the preview browser.

items.description: Messages and context. Give the agent a task in the composer. Add files, quote a previous response, or include a skill when the task needs more context.

items.description: Cursor. Cursor V2 runs through the official [`@cursor/sdk`](https://cursor.com/docs/api/sdk/typescript) TypeScript package. It does not use Cursor's ACP transport for V2 execution.

items.title: docs/user/default-browser.md
items.description: Use T3 Code as your default browser. On macOS, the desktop app can be your default web browser. Links you open from other apps then open in T3 Code. items.title: docs/user/devices.md
items.description: Devices. The Device panel shows a live iOS Simulator or Android Emulator next to a thread, so you can watch an agent verify mobile work and tap the device yourself. Agents get the same device through `device_*` tools and the `agent-device` command line, which T3 Code sets up for them.

items.title: docs/user/guest-links.md
items.description: Guest links. A guest link lets a teammate follow one thread in their browser and ask the agent questions, with no account. They see your messages and the agent's replies as they stream. Each message they send waits until you send or dismiss it.

items.description: Install T3 Code. T3 Code runs coding agents on your computer and lets you control them from its desktop, web, or mobile app. Set up the machine where the agents will work first.

items.title: docs/user/keybindings.md
items.description: Keybindings. Customize shortcuts in **Settings → Keybindings** on web and desktop. That page also lists the command IDs and defaults available in your version.

items.description: Keyboard focus. The command palette keeps focus while open. Closing it returns focus to the composer. items.title: docs/user/permission-modes.md
items.description: Permission modes. Permission modes control when an agent needs your approval to act. Choose a mode in the message composer; it applies to that thread.

items.title: docs/user/portable-handoffs.md
items.description: Context in portable handoffs. T3 Code transfers conversation context when you switch providers, continue through a portable restart, or use a fork that the provider cannot resume itself.

items.title: docs/user/project-settings.md
items.description: Settings and project overrides. On web and desktop, the "Applying settings for …" sentence at the top of Settings pages picks the project and environment a change applies to. items.title: docs/user/prompt-links.md
items.description: Prompt links. A prompt link opens T3 Code with a prompt ready to send. Use one to share a prompt on social media, or to put a one-click fix in a pull request comment.

items.title: docs/user/providers-acp.md
items.description: ACP providers. T3 Code can run installed ACP commands or coding agents from the official [ACP Registry](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/registry). Registry agents bring their own models, tools, and sign-in, while T3 Code provides projects, threads, checkpoints, and task delegation.

items.title: docs/user/providers-antigravity.md
items.description: Antigravity. T3 Code runs Google's official Antigravity ACP agent on your selected environment. It has its own sign-in, separate from the Antigravity IDE or CLI. Google controls which models and account access are available through this agent.

items.title: docs/user/providers-claude.md
items.description: Claude. T3 Code uses Claude Code's login and configuration. Start with the default provider for one account; [provider setup](./install.md#providers) covers installation and shared provider settings.

items.title: docs/user/providers-codex.md
items.description: Codex. Use your ChatGPT plan or an existing Codex CLI login to code in T3 Code.

items.title: docs/user/providers-muse.md
items.description: Muse Code. Muse Code is a beta integration and is disabled by default. Install [Muse Code](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code) on the machine hosting your environment, then run `muse login` as the account that runs T3 Code.

items.title: docs/user/providers-opencode.md
items.description: OpenCode. Install and authenticate OpenCode on the machine running your environment, then enable it in **Settings > Providers**. See [provider setup](./install.md#providers). T3 Code requires OpenCode 1.14.19 or newer, including when you connect an existing OpenCode server.

items.title: docs/user/providers-pi.md
items.description: Pi. T3 Code can use your existing Pi coding agent installation while keeping Pi's models, auth, extensions, skills, context files, and native session history.

items.title: docs/user/question-attachments.md
items.description: Files in question answers. When an agent asks a question that accepts a custom answer, use **Attach files** or paste an image into the answer field. On mobile, use the attachment button to choose photos or files. You can send a file by itself, with a selected option, or with a typed answer.

items.title: docs/user/remote-access.md
items.description: Remote access. Connect a phone, browser, or another desktop app to T3 Code running on a different machine. That machine must stay running and reachable while you work.

items.title: docs/user/snap-shot.md
items.description: SnapShots. A SnapShot captures the window you are working in and attaches it to your current draft. The attachment carries the app name and window title, and when available the app icon and the window's accessibility data (its controls, text, and their positions in the image). Agents can use that data to reason about…

items.title: docs/user/source-control.md
items.description: Source control. T3 Code integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, Gitea, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, and GitCafe to clone and publish repositories, create pull requests, and review changes.

items.description: Product usage data. The T3 Code server sends product usage events to T3 Code's own endpoint at `ingest.t3.codes`, associated with a hashed account or installation identifier. items.title: docs/user/terminal.md
items.description: Terminal history. Each terminal keeps up to 5,000 lines and 8 MiB of scrollback on its environment server. T3 Code removes the oldest output when either limit is reached. A long line can be shortened at the start. New terminal output is not truncated.

items.title: docs/user/thread-migration.md
items.description: Threads from older T3 Code versions. On your first V2 launch, T3 Code copies the V1 database, `state.sqlite`, into `statev2.sqlite` in the same data directory and migrates the copy. Your threads appear automatically, with full transcripts imported as needed. You do not need to run an import command.

items.title: docs/user/thread-sidebar.md
items.description: Working with threads. Use a new thread for a separate task. Choose **New worktree** when its code changes need a separate branch and working directory.

items.title: docs/user/updating.md
items.description: Updating T3 Code. The app you use and the server running your agents can be on different machines. When a server is behind your web or desktop app, an update notice appears in the conversation and **Settings → Connections**. Update the machine named in that notice.

items.title: docs/user/usage.md
items.description: Usage and limits. Open **Usage** from the sidebar or the command palette, or press `mod+u` on web and desktop when the terminal is not focused. Customize `usage.open` in **Settings → Keybindings**.

items.title: docs/user/voice-bridge.md
items.description: Voice bridge. Ask T3 Code from FluidVoice's notch. FluidVoice's Command window already turns a dictated instruction into an OpenAI chat request; this bridge answers that request by starting a real T3 thread and streaming the agent's answer back into the same window.

items.title: docs/user/welcome-wizard.md
items.description: Welcome wizard. T3 Code shows a setup flow when you open a new installation. Existing workspaces skip this flow.

items.title: Decision choice questions need two labels
items.description: A choice question with a single option passes schema but the classifier throws; the foundation now rejects it before encoding (a412a7ae).

items.title: Failed attempts keep cost unknown
items.description: A failed or unobserved model call has unknown spend, not zero; any total that includes one stays unknown and reports the known part separately.

items.title: Score against each labeler alone
items.description: Report results under the adjudicated labels and under each labeler alone; a ranking that flips under one labeler is not robust.

items.title: Run identity must hash the entry point
items.description: A retained run's identity must hash every executable source including the command-line entry point and provenance helper, or the result can describe different code.

items.title: Regular synthetic corpora only support revise
items.description: A corpus written by one author with regular structure can recommend revise at most; keep real incidents and hard negatives in the held-out set.

items.title: slipjay audit cause writes state
items.description: Only `slipjay audit status` is read-only. `slipjay audit cause` and the other setters change audit records and are out of scope for agents running an evaluation.

items.title: Prepared node_modules can miss vfile files
items.description: A prepared workspace can lack vfile 6.0.3 files (SJ-194); repair the generated package locally with an integrity check, with no source or shared-store change.

items.title: A rescore keeps the original run identity
items.description: Re-scoring retained records must not alter the run identity; it records the scorer digest that produced the new numbers.

items.title: Decision calls are limited to 60 a minute
items.description: DecisionService admits 60 calls a minute and 4 at once; evaluation runs use a fixed gap between calls and never retry automatically.

items.title: Never kill a process by name match
items.description: Your own agent's argv contains the path, so pkill -f or a pgrep pipeline can kill it; stop only a PID captured at spawn.

items.title: ~/.t3/userdata is the running installation
items.description: Copy from it; never open it read-write, clean it up, or start a server against it, and never symlink test data back to it.

items.title: Never set VITE_HTTP_URL or VITE_WS_URL in dev
items.description: Vite proxies /api, /ws and /oauth through the browser origin; a baked-in localhost breaks remote clients.

items.title: Landed work is not running until installed
items.description: A change landed on t3peach is not in the Nightly app until the t3-fork-install steps have run.

items.title: Cleanups and bumps are chores
items.description: A cleanup, dependency bump, dead-code removal or follow-up to just-landed work is done directly as a change, with no Spec, Ticket or Spec review.

items.title: Small pilots make no significance claim
items.description: With about thirty cases the 95% intervals overlap; report counts with intervals and avoid significance claims.

items.title: A Killed exit was the change, not the machine
items.description: A check that died with Killed looked like an environment failure but an unbounded buffer added by the change caused it; read the change before dismissing.

items.title: A fixture failed once its date aged out
items.description: A saved-usage fixture failed every commit after it passed the 92-day scan cache window (8c12bfaf41); keep fixture dates inside the window.

items.title: DPoP must use the https URL behind the tunnel
items.description: Behind the T3 Connect tunnel the client signs the https URL; verification must rebuild it from forwarded headers, not use the internal http URL.

items.title: Reused sessions must refresh MCP credentials
items.description: Reusing a provider session without refreshing MCP account credentials makes tools fail after token expiry.

items.title: Read-only tasks need an enforcing provider
items.description: A read-only managed task may run only on a provider that actually enforces read-only access; otherwise it must be refused.

items.title: Pending turn item reads need the partial index
items.description: Shell snapshot reads of pending turn items must go through the partial index; a full scan made streaming slow.

items.title: Record every deliberate upstream difference
items.description: Every deliberate difference from upstream updates fork/differences.md in the same change.

items.title: Default to no code comments
items.description: Record only a constraint, external quirk or invariant the code cannot show, in one to four lines.

items.title: UI components own their look
items.description: Exports in components/ui take a variant or size; do not restyle them through className.

items.title: Mobile navigation is separate from web
items.description: Shared client logic belongs in packages/client-runtime; mobile navigation is its own surface.

items.title: One integrated browser check after integration
items.description: A visible UI change gets one Browser-panel check by the primary agent after integration; helpers do not start dev servers.

items.title: Look-and-feel changes wait for the owner's yes
items.description: A change judged by look or feel is shown on a preview and lands only after the owner says it feels right; apply each round of notes to the same preview.

items.title: Avoid continuously repainting animations
items.description: Continuous repaints cost battery and frames on high-refresh displays; prefer transitions that settle.

items.title: A managed task waits a bounded time on background work
items.description: A managed task publishes its result after a bounded wait on a background command it left running; it never waits indefinitely.

items.title: A follow-up keeps the task's own workspace
items.description: A delegate_task follow-up continues in the existing conversation and workspace; do not start a fresh workspace for it.

items.title: A registered flaky test with a new error is not a known flake
items.description: A test in the flake registry that fails with a different error than the registered signature needs investigation, not a quarantine.

items.title: Unattended runs ask no routine questions
items.description: When the owner is away, settle reversible choices from evidence, record blocked actions and carry on with independent work.
